docs(evidence): anchor the Q27 manifest row to decision 0005 (#618)

The row cited the 2026-08-18 ruling set by session only, because
decision 0005 was not yet committed. Anchor it to
docs/midgard/decisions/0005-owner-rulings-2026-08-18.md R8. Manifest
quality verifier unchanged before/after: 9 defects (1 F05, 8 Q39/Q40).

docs(decisions): record the 2026-08-18 owner ruling set as decision 0005

R1-R9 as ruled in the 2026-08-18 session, including the R4 fulfillment
addendum (both reference-script wirings, measured 13,294/12,810
frontiers, owner-signed 12,810) and the issue dispositions. Renumbered
from 0004, which the flat-reversion decision already holds.

test(fault-proofs): correct two pre-calibration draft labels in the #622 evidence trail

The exact-frontier+1 journey's proof-fit headline named the calibration
item 14,019 instead of the committed probe item 14,005, and the reserve
file's constant-rows comment listed the calibration pair 14,018/14,019
instead of the committed 14,004/14,005. Labels and comments only; no
assertion changes.

test(fault-proofs): measure the post-Option-B frontiers and ExUnits through full emulator journeys (#622)

Three committed probe suites, every pin a build-sign-submit measurement:

- direct reserve frontier: item 13,522 signs the observe door at exactly
  the 15,872-byte reliability budget; the adjacent item 13,523 signs at
  15,873 and still completes to award — since Option B the reserve line is
  a cost line, not the pre-change liveness cliff.
- direct exact frontier: item 14,004 signs at 16,369 (last contiguous fit
  inside the 16,384-byte envelope); item 14,005 is refused pre-sign at a
  projected 16,385 and completes by the automatic publication fallback.
  The header records the measured quantization ladder above the frontier
  (the balancing fixed point makes signed size nonmonotone in item bytes;
  no item in this family signs at exactly 16,384).
- reference route at its own frontier, the tier-1 ceiling 14,336:
  publication 15,135 + five stages + award = 162,657 bytes end-to-end;
  one payload byte further is tier-2 carriage and cannot stage at all
  (deferred to #617's tiers revival). Plus the like-for-like baseline at
  the sweep's own shape (item 8,277): observe bytes identical at 10,463
  with cpu 299,480,995 vs the pre-change 574,227,003 (-47.8%), and
  authenticate/prepare collapsed to item-size-independent 2,656/1,864
  bytes; untouched stages bill byte- and unit-identically.

The owner-signed consensus-profile pins (12,810 / 13,294 / 5,000 / 14,336)
stay byte-untouched: rebinding them is #619's pending owner question, and
these suites are the measured table that decision consumes.

test(fault-proofs): capture every staged lifecycle transaction for the #622 measurement campaign

The route-freedom journey now records a labeled measurement for each
transaction it stages before the semantic leg (setup, the four
reference-script publications, init, open, source, the bisection reveals,
enter/prepare-resolution, prepare-selected), exposed as
`lifecycleMeasurements` on the journey. Two campaign helpers ride along:
a MIDGARD_PRINT_PROOF_FIT-gated one-line JSON dump of a journey's complete
measured table, and a 3%-band execution-unit pin for stages whose bill
wobbles run to run because on-chain out-ref lookups compare run-dependent
txids (measured on the reference route: authenticate 163,390 vs 166,458
memory units in consecutive runs).

Additive only: both #621 route-freedom suites re-run green (3/3 each).

test(validation): adversarial route matrix for the Option B complete-item chain (#621)

Hostile probes red, honest continuations green, against the applied
validators on one seeded emulator ledger: the retired four-field Verify
wire and a thread committing the old two-part (transition, auxiliary)
evidence hash are refused at the authenticate boundary, as is a
well-formed transition that is not the committed one; at the §8.8 door,
corrupted inline bytes, a publication bound to the wrong transaction
commitment, and a publication carrying perturbed preimage bytes are each
refused, then the same machinery passes with honest material on both
routes.

Two threads ride the same content — one inline, one by publication — and
their observed datums are pinned byte-identical to each other and to the
off-chain staging (route determinism, the property that makes #621's
routing a cost decision). The inline observe and the datum-corruption
probe are driven by a wallet that is not fraud_prover: valid data
succeeds to the identical state, invalid data fails, whoever carries it.
The mixed-driver thread continues to settlement, every transaction inside
the 16,384-byte envelope. Skips loudly under a pre-Option-B blueprint.

test(fault-proofs): drive the #621 route flips, envelope fallback, and publication recoveries to award

Four full emulator lifecycles over the production dispute builder, real
applied validators, local UPLC evaluation, sign and submit throughout:

- a heuristically-inline item forced onto the reference route (after the
  inline-plus-out-ref contradiction refuses off-chain, thread untouched);
- a heuristically-reference item forced inline (after a never-existed
  out-ref refuses off-chain naming both recoveries), with the pre-sign
  projection pinned byte-identical to the signed observe transaction;
- the largest tier-1 item the fixture family stages (14,324 bytes)
  requested inline: refused pre-sign at the 16,384-byte envelope
  (projected 16,540) and completed by the automatic mid-chain publication
  fallback on the same staged thread;
- a genuinely spent publication out-ref recovered by re-publishing the
  content-addressed publication up front.

Every journey pins the per-transaction reference-input counts, the L1
envelope on every submitted transaction, and runs the dispute to award;
arm-reachability bookkeeping refuses a silently-vacuous suite. Both files
skip loudly under a pre-Option-B blueprint, where every journey would
merely reproduce the recorded prepare-selected red.

test(fault-proofs): correct the reference row's stale pre-#620 reference-input pin (#621)

The recorded reference row pinned [0,2,0,2,0,0] — a proof-item reference
beside the authenticate stage as well as at the observe door. That value
dates from the row's creation and matched 8fe3052e (#617 item 1), whose
builder forwarded the publication into the authenticate stage; fc3817ff
(#620) dropped that forwarding without the pin ever becoming falsifiable,
because under the deployed pre-Option-B blueprint the row dies at
prepare-selected (the accepted 'Spend[0] unexpected empty list' red)
before this assertion is reached. Under an Option B blueprint the builder
— base b312ba1c included, before any #621 change — dereferences the
publication exactly once, at the observe stage's §8.8 door: [0,1,0,2,0,0].
The row's expected-red signature under the deployed blueprint is
untouched.

test(fault-proofs): pin the build-time delivery-route resolver's arms and boundary (#621)

Route precedence (explicit request over supplied out-ref over the
12,810-byte heuristic, measured at the boundary on both sides), the
inline-plus-out-ref contradiction refusal, the impossible-size propagation
of the single-publication ceiling, and the envelope-refusal error's
recorded projection fields.

feat(fault-proofs): resolve the §8.8 door's delivery route at build time with envelope fallback (#621)

Since Option B (#619/#620) no carriage index is frozen into evidence_hash,
so how a tier-1 complete item's preimage reaches the observe stage's door
is a build-time routing decision: an explicit proofItemDelivery request
wins, then a supplied publication out-ref, then the owner-signed
12,810-byte maxReliableDirectCompleteItemBytes measurement as a plain cost
heuristic. The pre-submit carriage assertion re-scopes accordingly, from
committed-index re-checking to build-time resolution against the door
transaction's own reference-input set (the SDK door re-checker's docs and
refusal message follow).

An inline build that outgrows the 16,384-byte L1 proof envelope is refused
pre-sign — by the dummy-witness projection when the provider ceiling sits
above the envelope, or translated from CML's own fee-build size refusal
when it does not (today's L1 parameters exactly) — and demotes to the §8
publication route mid-chain, so no routing input can strand a staged
thread. A spent or missing publication out-ref refuses off-chain, before
any stage transaction exists, naming both recoveries: re-publish the
content-addressed publication, or deliver inline.

docs(sdk,validation): retire the carriage-committed-evidence framing from the seam comments

Review findings 2-3 on the #620 implementation, plus one site the review
missed (validation-machine.ts): comments and two error messages still
described the auxiliary as hashed into the committed evidence_hash at
prepare and referenced the deleted VerifyReference route. Under the
transition-only commitment (#619) the tier is a build-time delivery
decision the observe-stage door verifies by content, and the reference
wrap happens at ObserveReference. No behavior change; carriage-seam and
proof-fit suites 11/11, typecheck+lint green in both packages.

feat(sdk,fault-proofs,validation): retire the by-hash and carriage staged wires in the TypeScript twins (#620)

The canonical-decode prepare schema collapses to the single four-field
transition-only arm and the item-semantic encoder to the generic
three-field Verify: the by-evidence-hash arm, the carriage redeemer
field, the VerifyReference reference-input route, and the staged
pipeline's proof-item forks are deleted rather than bypassed, and the
staged resolver-0 commitment hashes NoAuxiliaryWitness whatever carriage
the auxiliary names. A chunk-shaped auxiliary now refuses fail-closed at
redeemer construction: the retired four-field wire was the only shape it
could ever have ridden. The shared five-field PrepareSelected schema for
the other eleven phases and the direct-resolve route are untouched.

Tests pin the new wires raw (the committed blueprint moves once, in the
wave's regeneration): the proof-fit fit measurement moves to the observe
stage's inline Observe arm, which now carries the preimage; the
carriage-policy row pins the transition-only source text and the
observe routes; the emulator proof-fit harness deliberately keeps
speaking the deployed wire until the regeneration flips it.

test(validation): pin the transition-only item commitment in the cross-language one-step fixture (#620)

The generator now derives the item-path vector three ways and refuses to
emit on any disagreement: the TypeScript transition-only hash must equal
the base evidence hash (the commitment is over (transition,
NoAuxiliaryWitness)), the retired carriage-committed preimage must
differ from it, and the emitted Aiken test re-checks both equalities on
the other side of the language boundary. The base vectors are
byte-identical to the previous emission, so the producer did not drift.

test(fraud-proofs): prove every transition-only guard can fail across the staged item pipeline (#620)

Thirteen positives walk a genuine field-6 item journey through prepare,
authenticate, and observe under the narrowed commitment; twenty-three
hostile negatives were each run bare (fail markers stripped) against the
full suite to prove the guard they target actually fires: retired-wire
decode refusals for both prepare arms and both semantic arms, swapped
work witnesses and successors, the retired carriage-committed hash, a
substituted certified chunk, flipped carriage bytes on every observe
route, and the deleted observe conjunct's control. Constructor indices
are pinned after the arm retirement with golden wire-layout vectors.

feat(fraud-proofs): narrow the canonical-decode complete-item evidence commitment to the transition alone (#620)

Option B, scoped (spec #619): the prepare stage commits to
hash_one_step_evidence(transition, NoAuxiliaryWitness), computed on-chain;
the by-hash prepare arm and the authenticate stage's carriage argument,
reference-delivery arm, publication-reconstruction helper, and proof-item
parameter are retired; the observe stage keeps both delivery arms and drops
the frozen-hash equality, leaving the section-8.8 field door as the sole
content gate. No shared-library changes. Scratch ABI diff against the fork
baseline moves exactly the three validators (prepare 1788df9b->155131d4,
item-semantic a8d8f3ac->dc88d18e with params 3->2, observe
df695946->146db088); 408 other handler entries unchanged.
